func_80033024_33C24.title: Scan an attack-task subtree against a victim subtree
func_80033024_33C24.summary: Decodes active native attack spheres and tests them against a selected victim-task group.
behavior: Walks linked tasks beginning at attackers, stopping when a subsequent task priority at +0x20 is no greater than the starting priority. The links therefore delimit the native task subtree.
Requires a kind-2 render object at task +0x18, a nonzero attack descriptor at +0x48, an empty incoming contact pointer at +0x38, and outgoing collision bit 0x02 at byte +0x30.

Descriptor 0xFFFFFFFF selects a fixed sphere: unsigned radius at task +0x4E, signed Y/Z offsets at +0x50/+0x52, and zero X offset. Other descriptors resolve through the render object segment bindings and interpolate the sphere data using object animation frame +0x28.

Before each call to func_80033404_34004, writes local sphere X/Y/Z/radius to D_80168F80_169B80 through D_80168F8C_169B8C. One task can supply several spheres, and the scene coordinator can visit the same sphere again for another victim group.
cautions: Both list pointers must describe initialized live native task groups. The implementation reads starting priority before its null check.
This is a stateful contact scan, not an isolated geometry query. Do not run it a second time merely to observe attacks.
A descriptor or action ID alone does not establish an active hit. Observe the decoded sphere at its native call boundary and avoid counting repeated victim-group scans as new attacks.

func_80033404_34004.title: Test the current native attack sphere
func_80033404_34004.summary: Tests the sphere decoded by the attack-group scanner against eligible victim tasks.
behavior: At entry, four float scratch globals hold the current attacker-local X/Y/Z/radius. func_80033024_33C24 initializes them for both animated melee volumes and fixed projectile volumes.

The overlap path scales the offsets by object +0x1C/+0x20/+0x24, rotates them with func_80033898_34498 using the masked 10-bit rotations at +0x14/+0x16/+0x18, and adds world position at +0x08/+0x0C/+0x10. Attack radius is multiplied by object scale X.

Victim eligibility requires an appropriate incoming collision flag, a distinct kind-2 render object, no existing task +0x38 incoming hit, and nonzero body radius at +0x3C. Ordinary incoming bit 0x01 and special filtered incoming bit 0x04 are separate paths.

An overlap writes the victim task pointer to attacker +0x34, the attacker pointer to victim +0x38, and the current one-based sphere index to victim byte +0x44. The scan stops once attacker +0x34 is nonzero. This function does not itself subtract health.

The native body test uses radius at task +0x3C times object scale X and height at +0x3E times scale Y. For nonzero height it expands the X/Z radius by the attack sphere radius and checks the sphere against the body Y interval.
cautions: The scratch sphere belongs to the current scan only. Copy it at entry; do not retain its contents as a later frame or another attacker state.
Adding arbitrary tasks to native victim lists consumes hit records and can alter projectile or enemy callbacks. A read-only observer should leave task +0x34/+0x38 untouched.
The victim pointer must be a live initialized list; its priority is read before a null check.
Radius zero should not be promoted to a damaging body-proximity event by an observer. Health, invulnerability, ownership and hit deduplication remain separate concerns.

func_80033898_34498.title: Rotate a vector using native object angles
func_80033898_34498.summary: Applies the native three-axis rotation transform to caller-owned X/Y/Z floats.
func_80033898_34498.declaration: extern void func_80033898_34498(unsigned short rx, unsigned short ry, unsigned short rz, float *x, float *y, float *z);
behavior: Receives three unsigned 16-bit angle values followed by three writable float pointers. The vector is updated in place; there is no return value.
Native contact code masks object rotation halfwords to 0x03FF before this call. A full turn spans 1024 angle units.
This helper rotates only. Callers separately apply component scale before rotation and translation afterward.
cautions: The three float pointers must be valid writable storage. Do not pass task fields in place unless modifying that native state is intended.
This is the forward rotation used for attacker-local offsets. Victim-space conversion uses a different inverse helper.

func_801F77F4_5B3704.title: Run scene contacts and player-state maintenance
func_801F77F4_5B3704.summary: Native scene callback that coordinates contact scans between task groups and performs additional scene-state checks.
behavior: The native callback saves two scheduler arguments. Its inspected body obtains the task-group pointers from scene globals instead of using those arguments for contact selection.
After scene preparation, invokes func_80033024_33C24 for selected attacker/victim groups. While the player-manager pointer is live, four calls use D_801FC600_5B8510 as the outgoing attacker subtree.
Other pairs test actor and projectile groups against the playable-player group. The callback subsequently processes height, scene-exit and related state; it has effects beyond hit detection.
cautions: Observe the normal scheduler invocation. Calling the callback again repeats stateful scene work.
The callback belongs to its native gameplay overlay and requires initialized scene managers. A hook that ignores the scheduler arguments may declare no parameters.

D_801FC600_5B8510.title: Player-manager task subtree root
D_801FC600_5B8510.summary: Pointer to the native player-manager task used as the root of player contact scans.
behavior: The scene contact coordinator passes this pointer as the root attacker or victim list. Linked tasks with greater priority belong to the scanned subtree.
This root is distinct from D_801FC604_5B8514, the current playable-player task. An outgoing player-group scan can include owned projectile children as well as the playable actor.
Inspected projectile constructors store the owning playable-player task at projectile +0x5C. For a playable task itself, +0x5C instead points to player work; those layouts must not be confused.
cautions: Validate the current gameplay scene and task lifetime. A retained pointer is not a durable identity across scene transitions.
Group membership alone does not identify an individual attack owner; use the live playable task and verified projectile ownership fields when attribution matters.

D_80168F80_169B80.title: Current native attack sphere X offset
D_80168F80_169B80.summary: Float scratch storage for the current attack sphere x offset in attacker-local units.
behavior: The native attack scanner writes this value immediately before func_80033404_34004 tests the decoded sphere. Animated descriptors use the render object animation frame; descriptor 0xFFFFFFFF supplies a fixed task sphere.
Scale the three local offsets by their respective object scales, rotate with the native object transform, then add object world position to obtain the sphere center.
This mutable scratch value is overwritten for every sphere and victim-group scan. It is not a persistent property of the current player.
cautions: Read at the native sphere-test entry boundary and copy the value before using it elsewhere.
The address holds one float, not a pointer or an enumerated flag.

func_801D9E9C_595DAC.title: Process native player damage and contact reactions
func_801D9E9C_595DAC.summary: Handles death state, environmental hazards and the incoming native contact for a fully initialized playable player.
behavior: Checks zero health, floor hazards and crushing before consulting the attacker pointer at player task +0x38. A nonzero result therefore does not identify a particular contact or prove health was lost.

For an ordinary type-1 attacker, reads attacker +0x18 as an object pointer, byte +0x4C as hit kind and byte +0x6D as damage. The object world X/Y/Z at +0x08/+0x0C/+0x10 establish hurt direction. One damage unit is the ordinary half-heart baseline.

Routes ordinary hits through native armour, player action/context, health loss, hurt animation and direction handling. Sudden Impact vulnerability can double the health loss. An armour-blocked hit can start invulnerability even while the function returns zero.

The inspected type-1 paths do not retain their attacker descriptor. Type 2 is different: interaction paths can retain the attacker in player +0xE0. Do not generalize type-1 lifetime behavior to every hit kind.
The normal player pre-update calls func_801E8E24_5A4D34(player, 1) after a nonzero result to cancel eligible owned projectile tasks.
cautions: Requires the real playable task, live work/object/projectile-list fields and initialized gameplay/save state. A standalone visual actor is not a valid receiver.
The routine does not reproduce all of its caller availability checks. Normal intake is gated by work +0x69, the control-state bytes and native contact/invulnerability state.
An observer must preserve existing native attacker records and environmental-hit priority. A second call can process state changes beyond the intended contact.
Return value is a native reaction/cleanup indicator, not a damage amount or a complete accepted-hit boolean. Compare health and recovery state when those distinctions matter.
func_801D9E9C_595DAC.returns: Integer native reaction indicator. Nonzero triggers the normal caller's projectile cleanup; zero can still accompany armour absorption and newly started recovery.

func_801E8E24_5A4D34.title: Cancel eligible player-owned projectiles
func_801E8E24_5A4D34.summary: Marks selected projectiles in the playable player's owned task subtree for deferred removal.
func_801E8E24_5A4D34.declaration: extern void func_801E8E24_5A4D34(void *player, unsigned char reason);
behavior: Reads the owned-projectile manager through player task +0xDC, follows its task links, and examines tasks while their priority exceeds the playable player's priority.
Uses each child's type byte at +0x64 to select the native cancellation table. Eligible entries are marked with byte +0x65 = 1 and byte +0x66 = reason.
The owned-projectile manager processes these marks during its ordinary updates. The normal damage caller supplies reason 1 after a nonzero intake result.
cautions: The player and its +0xDC manager must be live and initialized; the native function does not perform these pointer checks.
This mutates selected owned projectile tasks. It is not a generic task destructor and does not cancel every projectile type.

func_801CB824_587734.title: Run the playable-player pre-update
func_801CB824_587734.summary: Advances player animation and processes input, invulnerability, damage and action transitions before the player update callback.
behavior: Expects the scheduler's real playable task and its render object. Player work byte +0x69 gates the main body while character resources change.
Updates animation frame and input-derived state, then runs normal control and invulnerability maintenance when the low control bits permit it.
Calls func_801D9E9C_595DAC only when D_800C7AE2 and D_800C7AE3 are both zero and D_800C7AE0 equals 0 or 4. Calls func_801E8E24_5A4D34(player, 1) after a nonzero intake result.
An entry hook runs before these native updates. A return hook sees their resulting state; it cannot be treated as the same timing boundary.
cautions: Do not apply this playable callback to a remote visual object or call it twice to obtain a collision query.
Damage availability is narrower than the late collision callback's low-bit gate. Preserve the individual native byte checks instead of substituting a guessed action blacklist.

D_800C7AE2.title: Native player input and damage lock byte
D_800C7AE2.summary: A live control-state byte that blocks gameplay input copying and normal player damage intake.
behavior: Byte storage at g_system +0x3AE22. The exported symbol has no ROM suffix.
The native playable pre-update requires this byte to be zero before calling damage intake. It separately requires D_800C7AE3 to be zero and D_800C7AE0 to equal 0 or 4.
Other native paths also read and write this byte; the inspected damage gate does not establish a complete semantic enumeration for all of its values.

The native gameplay-input copier also requires this byte and D_800C7AE3 to be zero before copying raw buttons into the four derived controller records. The ordinary save-sign interaction uses value 1 while its native dialog owns player input.
cautions: This reproduces only the native control-byte gate. It does not validate a player, save, contact, resource transition or invulnerability timer.
Do not replace the one-byte declaration with a word or a pointer.

Native callers can set this lock before initializing a replacement scenario. A delayed cleanup must not clear a lock acquired by that replacement; input filtering and lock changes need explicit ownership and lifecycle boundaries.
